key_insight: PORTER represents EHR events from language descriptions plus numeric handling, making the model less dependent on a fixed clinical vocabulary.
clinical_relevance: This could make foundation models easier to transfer across hospitals and pipelines without extensive vocabulary harmonization while preserving prediction performance.
method: Uses a frozen text encoder to embed event descriptions instead of fixed event tokens.
Adds a dedicated pathway for numeric values to capture magnitude.
Learns patient-time dynamics with an autoregressively pretrained temporal backbone.
evidence_signal: Across 74 pediatric prediction tasks, PORTER matched a fixed-vocabulary model in mean AUROC, retained 97.1% of target-vocabulary performance on unseen descriptions, and outperformed the fixed-vocabulary model on MIMIC after vocabulary shift.
watch_item: Cross-site deployment still depends on how well local event descriptions and numeric formats are rendered into text-grounded inputs.
paper_title: PORTER: Language-Grounded Event Representations for Portable Structured EHR Foundation Models
